questions: Can the edge reversal operation be performed multiple times, and does each reversal toggle the direction of all edges (so two reversals restore original directions)?
Is the edge reversal operation allowed at any time, including when no outgoing edge exists from the current vertex, or only when there is at least one outgoing edge?
Does the reversal operation affect edges globally for the entire graph, or only locally relative to the current vertex?
Is the cost X incurred each time the reversal operation is performed, regardless of whether it changes reachable edges effectively?
Are self-loops (edges where u_i = v_i) allowed, and if so, do they behave normally under reversal?
Can we move along an edge and then immediately reverse edges in the same step, or are operations strictly sequential with one per iteration?
Is the goal to minimize total cost, or is any sequence of operations valid as long as vertex N is reached?
Does the reversal operation have any cooldown or limitation, such as not being allowed twice consecutively?
